facts.statement: Tienshanosaurus is an extinct genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived in China during the Late Jurassic.
facts.quote: Tienshanosaurus (meaning "Tienshan lizard") is an extinct genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic of what is now China.

facts.statement: Professor Yuan Fuli discovered the remains of approximately thirty adult and three juvenile sauropods in Xinjiang on September 11, 1928.
facts.quote: On 11 September 1928 Chinese geology professor Yuan Fuli ("P.L. Yüan") discovered in Xinjiang the remains of about thirty adult and three juvenile sauropods

facts.statement: Paleontologist Yang Zhongjian named the species Tienshanosaurus chitaiensis in 1937.
facts.quote: In 1937 paleontologist Yang Zhongjian ("C.C. Young") named the type species Tienshanosaurus chitaiensis.

facts.statement: The generic name Tienshanosaurus refers to the Tian Shan mountains, meaning "heavenly mountains".
facts.quote: The generic name, suggested by Yuan, refers to the Tian Shan, the "heavenly mountains".

facts.statement: The specific name chitaiensis refers to the location Chitai (or Qitai).
facts.quote: The specific name refers to the location Chitai or Qitai.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was found near Paikushan in the Shishugou Formation, which dates to the Oxfordian stage.
facts.quote: The holotype, IVPP AS 40002-3, was found near Paikushan, Luanshantze, in sandstone of the Shishugou Formation dating from the Oxfordian.

facts.statement: The known skeleton consists of postcranial elements, while the skull and lower jaws are missing.
facts.quote: It consists of elements of the postcrania. A considerable part of the skeleton is known but not the skull or the lower jaws.

facts.statement: The estimated body length of Tienshanosaurus is twelve meters.
facts.quote: The body length has been estimated at twelve metres.

facts.statement: Fossilized eggs were found among the sauropod remains discovered in Xinjiang.
facts.quote: The finds, including a fossilized egg, were sent to Beijing

facts.statement: Establishing the classification of Tienshanosaurus has been difficult due to the fragmentary nature of the fossil material.
facts.quote: Due to the fragmentary nature of the material and a limited description, it has not been easy to establish the affinities of Tienshanosaurus.

facts.statement: While originally placed in Helopodinae and later various other groups, recent consensus in 2011 assigns Tienshanosaurus to the family Mamenchisauridae.
facts.quote: Originally classified in the Helopodinae, it has been assigned to many groups, among them the Astrodontidae, Euhelopodidae, Brachiosauridae, and Camarasauridae, but recent consensus (2011) has been to assign Tienshanosaurus to Mamenchisauridae.

facts.statement: Tienshanosaurus lived during the Oxfordian stage, between 161.5 and 154.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Oxfordian to Oxfordian (161.5 to 154.8 million years ago)
